messages.subject: coordinates input
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I just have a basic question regarding the input of location coordinates for the micro_global function. In the help file it says "longitude and latitude"; would this mean I input longitude followed by latitude  (as in loc=" long, lat")? I have just had a bit of confusion since in google maps, latitude is followed by longitude when clicking on a point in the map.

Thanks,

Felix

messages.subject: Re: coordinates input
messages.body_plain:
Hi Dr. Kearney,

Thank you for your response. I have run a few test runs using coordinates that express a land location as (lat, long), but when reversed, show an ocean location. For example, I have found that inputting coordinates as (45.155, 0.546) in the microclimate model (a land locality if the order is latitude followed by longitude) works fine. However, if I reverse the coordinates and input them in the model as (0.546, 45.155), an ocean locality if the order is latitude followed by longitude, the model yields an error and cannot run.

I am thus beginning to think that perhaps coordinates should be entered in the model as loc=(lat, long) rather than loc=(long, lat). But perhaps I have made a mistake in these tests, so I was hoping you could confirm this with me.

Any thoughts on this?

Thank you,

Felix

messages.subject: Re: coordinates input
messages.body_plain:
Hi Felix,

It should work the same if you put e.g.

micro_global(loc = c(144.9633, -37.81411))

or

micro_global(loc = "Melbourne, Australia")

The micro_global script will check to see what you're using as input (text or lat/long) and use it accordingly.

The relevant code inside micro_global is below - you can try this out separately to see what's going wrong (the variable 'x' is what is ultimately used to query the global data sets):

    if(is.numeric(loc)==FALSE & length(loc)==1){
      # use geocode to get location from site name via googlemaps
      longlat <- dismo::geocode(loc)[3:4] # assumes first geocode match is correct
      if(nrow(longlat>1)){longlat<-longlat[1,]}
      x <- t(as.matrix(as.numeric(c(longlat[1,1],longlat[1,2]))))
    }else{
      if(is.numeric(loc)==FALSE){ # might not be quite right format, try correcting
        loc=cbind(as.numeric(loc[1]),as.numeric(loc[2]))
      }
      longlat <- loc
      x <- t(as.matrix(as.numeric(c(loc[1],loc[2]))))
    }

All the best,
Mike
